newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia blasts Canada pension changes.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia blasts Canada pension changes.

text.p: British Columbia on Friday criticized Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin's plans to revamp the Canada Pension Plan (CPP).

Provincial Finance Minister Andrew Petter said the changes were "unfair to low wage earners, the disabled and women and are being rushed through with the support of Quebec which is not a participant in the CPP."
British Columbia and Saskatchewan have sought to block Martin's steps.
Petter said the federal government's position was another example of its disregard for the West.

While there is consensus on the need to change the pension plan to make its financing more secure, the proposed changes require "the most vulnerable" in society to shoulder a disproportionate share of the burden, Petter said.

Martin's proposal calls for an increase in pension plan premiums to 9.9 percent of insurable earnings over the next six years from 5.85 percent. Ottawa had warned the fund would run out of money in less than 20 years without increases.

British Columbia contended the proposal "will significantly cut pension benefits for future seniors and in the years ahead, lower-income earners will pay the highest increases in their contribution rates. Disability pensions, death benefits and survivor benefits will all be reduced."
Petter said the vote of Quebec, where the CPP is not in effect, was used to ram the changes through and said this was an example of federal disregard for the West.
